title: Mexico and China Agree on Working Group to Boost Mexican Exports to China
author: La Jornada Editorial Staff
content:
_This article by[La Jornada Editorial
Staff](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/La) originally appeared in the
[November 23, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/23/economia/mexico-y-
china-acuerdan-mesa-de-trabajo-que-incluye-aumentar-exportaciones-al-pais-
asiatico), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

Economy Secretary Marcelo Ebrard and China’s Commerce Minister Wang Wentao
agreed this Monday in Beijing to establish a working group to address the
priorities of the bilateral economic agenda. Among the issues to be reviewed
are mechanisms to increase Mexico’s exports to that country.

According to a statement, the agreement emerged from the 11th Meeting of the
Mexico-China High-Level Group, which both officials chaired. The session
followed up on President Claudia Sheinbaum’s visit to the [Asia-Pacific
Economic Cooperation
(APEC)](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/19/economia/apec-2026-concluye-
cumbre-en-china-con-llamado-a-eliminar-barreras-comerciales-y-crear-zona-de-
libre-comercio) Leaders’ Summit and her meeting with President Xi Jinping,
held last week in Shenzhen, southern China.

Ebrard told his counterparts that trade between the two countries has a
**persistent and growing imbalance**. According to the figures he presented,
China will export **more than US$130 billion** to Mexico this year, while
Mexican sales to that market will total around **US$10 billion**.

## Ebrard Asks China to Approve Sanitary and Trade Protocols

The economy secretary called for narrowing that gap and requested faster
approval of sanitary and trade protocols that, in some cases, have remained
unresolved for a decade. These documents are necessary for Mexico to export
avocados, limes, beef, pork, sorghum and processed aquatic products, among
other goods.

![Mexican and Chinese delegations sit across a conference table during their
meeting in Beijing.](https://mexicosolidarity.com/wp-
content/uploads/2026/11/mexico-china-export-working-group-photo-1.webp)The
teams of China’s Commerce Minister Wang Wentao and Economy Secretary Marcelo
Ebrard during a meeting in Beijing, China. Photo: Secretariat of Economy.

Ebrard said the proposal seeks to close the difference between imports and
exports “decisively and quickly,” with Mexican sales growing at the same pace
as purchases from China have. He also invited his counterpart to move to
Mexico some of the production currently carried out in China and exported to
Mexico.

> “What I am proposing is to reduce this disparity between imports and exports
> decisively and quickly, maintaining the same pace of growth in our exports
> that we have had in our imports,” Secretary Ebrard said.

The working group will review, among other issues, the proposal from the
state-owned company Exportadora de Sal, which aims to expand its share of the
Chinese market. The company offered to supply **up to 10 million metric tons**
over the next four years.

Mexico’s participants also included Undersecretary of Foreign Trade Luis
Rosendo Gutiérrez; the head of the International Trade Negotiations Unit,
Deborah Alcocer; Exportadora de Sal Director Moisés Poblanno; and the Mexican
embassy’s chargé d’affaires, Sergio Kwiatek.
